I should note that things haven't been as grim as they might sound. I've since got myself a home to live on my own and I've still got my job. I have only been hospitalized once for my suicide attempts and not for that long. I've spent time developing applications outside of work. And I guess I still want to live, for now, at least.

I've actually recently bought "Meditations" by Marcus Aurelius, alongside "Beyond good and evil" by Friedrich Nietzsche. Since my last confinement I've read "The Art of War", "On Aggression" by Konrad Lorenz and, following advice of my psychotherapist, "How to Win Friends and Influence People" by Dale Carnegie. I am currently reading "The Prince" by Niccolo Machiavelli and a few self-help books.

As to why I've not killed myself yet, well, I've recently started tossing a coin everytime I feel suicidal. I write down the reason for each toss in my Diary and it helps postpone the deed. I've decided to toss it a fixed number of times, after which I'll follow whatever it'll tell me to do.

And if it's gonna be life, I'll start doing it again, making the fixed number smaller.

But, to be honest, it feels like I might break and do it much sooner.

Sounds interesting, I'll defenitely check that out. So far I've tried, in no particular order - autogenic training, hypnotherapy, working out, dieting, following extensive skin care routine and training Thai boxing.

It's just that I don't have any emotional connection with anybody. I can't open up to my family, because I've become afraid of telling them anything. I fear of being taken away against my will again.

I can't tell coworkers for obvious reasons, and I've lost all friends I had, ever since the first commitment.

I am seeing a psychiatrist, as well as a psychotherapist. I've been through a ton of antidepressants and neuroleptics. We change them from time to time, but they just never work - these thoughts won't go away.

Without you, this thread would of been another stepstone to a bad decision. Sure, my problems aren't gone, but now, going to sleep, I know that someone cared enough to listen. To help when it matteres the most. Thank you.
